item.vignette: Plasma from a patient with hereditary angioedema is incubated with sebetralstat. Kallikrein activity decreases rapidly, and generation of the vasoactive mediator responsible for increased vascular permeability is reduced.
item.lead_in: Which substrate-to-product reaction is most directly inhibited?

options.E: Complement C3 to C3a and C3b

item.tested_construct: Inhibition of plasma-kallikrein cleavage of high-molecular-weight kininogen to bradykinin
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Sebetralstat is a competitive, reversible inhibitor of plasma kallikrein. Plasma kallikrein cleaves high-molecular-weight kininogen and releases bradykinin; inhibition of this reaction reduces bradykinin generation and vascular permeability during hereditary angioedema attacks.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. Plasma kallikrein cleaves high-molecular-weight kininogen to release bradykinin, and sebetralstat inhibits this reaction.
distractor_explanations.B: Angiotensin-converting enzyme catalyzes conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II and is not the target of sebetralstat.
distractor_explanations.C: Plasminogen activation belongs to the fibrinolytic system rather than the kallikrein-kinin reaction targeted here.
distractor_explanations.D: Thrombin converts fibrinogen to fibrin and is not directly inhibited by sebetralstat.
distractor_explanations.E: Complement C3 cleavage is mediated by complement convertases, not plasma kallikrein in this therapeutic mechanism.

explanation.educational_objective: Connect plasma kallikrein inhibition with reduced cleavage of high-molecular-weight kininogen and reduced bradykinin formation in hereditary angioedema.

item.vignette: Fibroblast-lineage cells from fibrotic lung tissue are exposed to nerandomilast. Expression of profibrotic growth factors decreases after preferential inhibition of a phosphodiesterase isoenzyme that normally hydrolyzes a cyclic nucleotide.
item.lead_in: Which intracellular change most directly follows this enzyme inhibition?
item.tested_construct: Elevation of intracellular cyclic AMP after preferential PDE4B inhibition
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Nerandomilast preferentially inhibits phosphodiesterase 4B. PDE4 hydrolyzes and inactivates cyclic AMP; therefore PDE4B inhibition elevates intracellular cyclic AMP and contributes to reduced profibrotic and inflammatory signaling.

distractor_explanations.A: PDE4 inhibition prevents cyclic AMP hydrolysis, so cyclic AMP rises rather than falls.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. Preferential PDE4B inhibition decreases cyclic AMP degradation and raises intracellular cyclic AMP.
distractor_explanations.C: PDE4 acts on cyclic AMP rather than cyclic GMP.
distractor_explanations.D: IP3 is generated by phospholipase C signaling and is not the immediate product of PDE4B inhibition.
distractor_explanations.E: DAG is also generated by phospholipase C and is not the second-messenger change caused directly by PDE4B inhibition.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize that PDE4B inhibition decreases cyclic AMP hydrolysis and therefore increases intracellular cyclic AMP.

item.vignette: Neutrophils from a patient with WHIM syndrome carry a gain-of-function CXCR4 variant and show excessive retention in bone marrow. After mavorixafor treatment, mature neutrophils and lymphocytes increase in peripheral blood.
item.lead_in: Which receptor-ligand interaction is directly blocked to produce this mobilization?
item.tested_construct: Blockade of CXCR4 binding to CXCL12, reducing marrow retention of leukocytes
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Mavorixafor is a CXCR4 antagonist that blocks binding of CXCL12, also called stromal-derived factor-1. CXCR4-CXCL12 signaling promotes leukocyte homing and retention in bone marrow; antagonism mobilizes mature neutrophils and lymphocytes into the circulation.

distractor_explanations.A: CCR5-CCL5 signaling participates in leukocyte trafficking but is not the interaction directly blocked by mavorixafor.
distractor_explanations.B: CXCR2-CXCL8 signaling promotes neutrophil chemotaxis and is not the WHIM-associated receptor-ligand pair.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. Mavorixafor blocks CXCR4-CXCL12 signaling and thereby releases leukocytes from marrow retention.
distractor_explanations.D: CCR7-CCL19 is important for lymphoid-organ trafficking rather than the CXCR4-mediated myelokathexis mechanism.
distractor_explanations.E: S1P1 regulates lymphocyte egress from lymphoid tissue but is not the direct target of mavorixafor.

explanation.educational_objective: Link WHIM syndrome myelokathexis to excessive CXCR4-CXCL12 signaling and explain leukocyte mobilization by CXCR4 antagonism.

item.vignette: Vascular smooth-muscle cells are exposed to endothelin-1 in the presence of aprocitentan. Endothelin-dependent vasoconstrictive and proliferative signaling is suppressed. Receptor-binding studies show that the drug is not selective for only one endothelin receptor subtype.
item.lead_in: Which receptor profile is directly antagonized?

options.A: Angiotensin II AT1 and AT2 receptors

item.tested_construct: Dual antagonism of endothelin ETA and ETB receptors
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Aprocitentan is an endothelin receptor antagonist that inhibits endothelin-1 binding to both ETA and ETB receptors. Endothelin signaling contributes to vasoconstriction, vascular remodeling, fibrosis, inflammation, and aldosterone synthesis in hypertension.

distractor_explanations.A: AT1 and AT2 are angiotensin II receptors and are not the direct targets of aprocitentan.
distractor_explanations.B: Adrenergic receptor antagonism would affect catecholamine signaling rather than endothelin-1 responses.
distractor_explanations.C: Vasopressin receptors mediate vascular and renal water-balance effects but are not the aprocitentan targets.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. Aprocitentan antagonizes both ETA and ETB endothelin receptors.
distractor_explanations.E: Steroid-hormone receptors are intracellular nuclear receptors and do not explain direct blockade of endothelin-1 signaling.

explanation.educational_objective: Differentiate dual endothelin ETA/ETB receptor antagonism by aprocitentan from other antihypertensive receptor mechanisms.

item.vignette: Respiratory syncytial virus is incubated with a long-acting human IgG1 monoclonal antibody before exposure to airway epithelial cells. Viral entry is reduced even though viral genome replication enzymes are not inhibited. The antibody binds a conserved epitope present on both pre-fusion and post-fusion forms of the viral fusion protein.
item.lead_in: Which direct action best explains the antiviral effect?

options.A: Inhibition of the RSV RNA-dependent RNA polymerase
options.B: Inhibition of viral protease cleavage of polyproteins
options.C: Blockade of the RSV G-protein attachment receptor interaction
options.D: Depletion of infected cells through CD20 binding
options.E: Binding antigenic site IV on RSV F protein to prevent viral-cell membrane fusion

item.tested_construct: Neutralizing binding to conserved antigenic site IV on RSV F protein, preventing membrane fusion and entry
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Clesrovimab-cfor is a neutralizing monoclonal antibody that targets the extracellular RSV fusion protein. It binds a conserved epitope on antigenic site IV of the F protein and prevents fusion of viral and cellular membranes, thereby blocking viral entry.

distractor_explanations.A: Polymerase inhibition acts after viral entry and is not the mechanism of this monoclonal antibody.
distractor_explanations.B: RSV does not rely on the described protease-targeting mechanism, and the antibody acts extracellularly before entry.
distractor_explanations.C: The documented direct target is the RSV F protein rather than blockade of a G-protein attachment interaction.
distractor_explanations.D: CD20 is a B-cell surface protein and has no role in direct RSV neutralization.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. Clesrovimab-cfor binds conserved antigenic site IV on RSV F protein and prevents viral-cell membrane fusion and entry.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize neutralization of RSV by antibody binding to antigenic site IV of the F protein and blockade of membrane fusion.
